title: App Surface Implementation Gate Closure Semantics
authorityNotice: This artefact records which app-surface gates are semantically closable from repository authority and which remain requires evidence by external proof, provider setup, store account evidence, compliance review, or owner acceptance. It does not authorise implementation/runtime code, provider account setup, credential setup, deployment, store submission, or readiness claims.

runtime proof collection required by the implementation directive

externalEvidenceRequirements.evidenceRequirement: Requires Apple account, signing, credential custody, app metadata, privacy label, privacy manifest, review evidence, and human approval evidence that are not present in repository authority.

Requires Google Play account, signing/key management, credential custody, release track, Data Safety, permission disclosure, Play Integrity, review evidence, and human approval evidence that are not present in repository authority.

Requires concrete provider selection, provider account evidence, DNS/TLS/domain evidence, environment and secret handling evidence, rollback/logging evidence, and deployment proof that are not present in repository authority.

Requires privacy compliance evidence, external review where applicable, store privacy disclosures, consent proof, retention/deletion/export proof, data inventory confirmation, and legal/compliance acceptance that are not present in repository authority.

Requires owner-selected external review evidence. Repository semantics can identify review requirements but cannot substitute for external privacy, legal, store policy, ads policy, security, accessibility, internationalisation, CDN/provider, or monetisation review.

Requires final owner acceptance after store, CDN, privacy, and external review gates are resolved or explicitly accepted as remaining evidence requirements. The owner approval in chat authorises agent decisions, but it does not create missing external proof evidence.
The parent gate is closed for bounded local implementation; external provisioning, privacy, external review, and owner acceptance remain evidence requirements for external readiness claims.
